messages.content: Hello, who are you?
I'm the LLM-Chain helper — I answer questions about training your own LLM locally. What do you want to know?
Hi there!
Hi! I'm the LLM-Chain helper. Ask me anything about local LLM fine-tuning.
What is LLM-Chain?
LLM-Chain is an open-source desktop app for fine-tuning language models on your own machine — no cloud, no API key, just your hardware.
What hardware do I need?
An Apple Silicon Mac (8 GB+ unified memory) or an NVIDIA GPU (8 GB+ VRAM) covers most cases. CPU-only works for tiny models (≤100M params).
What's LoRA?
LoRA — Low-Rank Adaptation — trains small adapter weights on top of a frozen base model. Much cheaper than full fine-tuning, and the adapter file is tiny (a few MB).
What's QLoRA?
QLoRA quantizes the base model to 4-bit so a 7B model fits in 8 GB VRAM, then trains LoRA adapters on top. Best size/quality tradeoff for consumer GPUs.
How do I export to GGUF?
Open the run in LLM-Chain, click Export to GGUF, pick a quant (q4_k_m is the recommended default). The resulting .gguf works in llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM Studio.
Which model should I start with?
For a quick smoke test on Apple Silicon, SmolLM2 360M Instruct or Qwen3 0.6B. Small, fast, and they have proper chat templates.
What's a chat template?
A chat template tells the tokenizer how to render a list of messages into a string the model was trained on. Base models don't have one, so they need plain text data instead.
Why did my training fail?
Most often: the model is a base checkpoint paired with chat-format data, or the dataset path is wrong. Check the error message in the run details — LLM-Chain forwards the underlying trainer output.
What dataset format should I use?
JSONL chat ({"messages": [...]}) for instruct-style fine-tuning. CSV or text-dir for plain-text. Hugging Face Hub IDs work too — no download step required.
How long does training take?
Depends on model size and dataset. A 0.6B-param LoRA on a few hundred chat rows takes ~1–5 minutes on an M-series Mac. 7B models with QLoRA take 30+ minutes.
Can I push my model to Hugging Face?
Yes — run `huggingface-cli login` once, then click Push to Hugging Face Hub on the run details. The adapter goes up; LLM-Chain never stores your token.
What's a good batch size?
Start at 1 and raise only if your device has VRAM headroom. Bigger batches = faster steps and more stable training, but more memory.
What learning rate should I use?
2e-4 (0.0002) is the standard LoRA default. Halve it if loss spikes; double it if loss plateaus too high.
What's LoRA rank?
Rank is the size of the low-rank adapter. Rank 8–16 covers most chat fine-tunes; 32–64 for harder tasks like style transfer or code.
Explain LoRA alpha.
Alpha scales how much the adapter influences the base model. Convention: alpha = 2 × rank. Don't tweak it separately unless you know why.
What is fine-tuning?
Fine-tuning teaches a pretrained model to follow a specific style, persona, or task by training on examples of the desired behavior. LLM-Chain uses LoRA / QLoRA to keep it cheap.
Can I cancel a run?
Yes — there's a Cancel button on the run details page. The trainer subprocess gets terminated; partial adapter weights are kept on disk if you want to resume later.
Where are runs saved?
Default is ~/.llm-chain/runs/<run-id>/. You can change the location in Settings — restart LLM-Chain after changing it.
What's the difference between LoRA and full fine-tuning?
Full fine-tuning updates every parameter (highest quality, very expensive). LoRA freezes the base and trains tiny adapter weights (much cheaper, slight quality hit, tiny output file).
Does LLM-Chain support multimodal models?
Yes — Qwen2-VL is in the registry. Pair a JSONL-chat-with-images dataset with a vision-language model and the picker auto-routes to the VLM trainer.
What's a VLM?
A vision-language model — a transformer that processes images and text together. Qwen2-VL, LLaVA, Idefics. LLM-Chain supports Qwen2-VL out of the box.
Can I train on CPU?
Yes, but only on tiny models (~100M params or less). The Dashboard exposes CPU as a selectable device when the cap is non-zero. Expect minutes per step.
How do I stop the loss from going up?
Spiking loss usually means the learning rate is too high. Halve it (2e-4 → 1e-4) and try again. Also check your dataset — corrupt rows can spike the loss.
What is GGUF?
GGUF is the file format used by llama.cpp and its descendants (Ollama, LM Studio). It packs weights, tokenizer, and metadata into a single file optimized for inference on CPUs and consumer GPUs.
Is the trained adapter portable?
Yes. The LoRA adapter is a few MB of safetensors plus a config — works anywhere peft works. Merging it into a GGUF gives you a standalone model file you can ship on its own.
What's q4_k_m?
q4_k_m is a 4-bit k-quantization in GGUF — best size/quality tradeoff for most users. Smaller than q8_0, slightly higher quality than q4_0. Good default.
Why isn't Pythia in the picker?
Pythia is a base model with no chat template — it can't tokenize JSONL-chat data. The picker hides it for chat datasets. Pair Pythia with a CSV or text-dir dataset instead.
Bye!
Take care! Happy fine-tuning.
